correctness.rationale: Each candidate variable occurs in at most two resident constraints and each resident tests the sum of at most two binary variables within an integer interval. Combining duplicate pair constraints reduces the dependency graph to disjoint paths/cycles; two-state dynamic programming gives feasible minimum L and maximum H in linear time. For any two feasible endpoint assignments, each forbidden mixed switch at opposite-sign changing sites becomes a directed implication; strongly connected components lie on sign-alternating paths or even cycles and change cardinality by at most one. Activating components in reverse condensation topological order preserves every local interval and sweeps all cardinalities between L and H. The 7-vertex three-arm exact-one construction yields feasible counts {1,3}, certifying a degree-three boundary. Independent exhaustive enumeration of 10843 path/cycle systems checked exact spectra; finite enumeration alone does not prove the SCC theorem.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks do not replace the stated infinite proof or establish correctness of assumptions outside the precise theorem domain.

evidence: General max-degree-two polynomial-time exact-k algorithms do not certify an all-k contiguous spectrum or O(V+E). Upper-bound-only linear time does not cover positive lower bounds.

originality.rationale: Knop–Schierreich previously solved degree-two housing with arbitrary approval sets in polynomial time. Schierreich previously gave a linear-time algorithm only for upper-bound approvals, where deletion closure makes gap freedom trivial. Exact interval [ell,u] with positive lower bounds, a complete cardinality spectrum and a linear-time arbitrary-k constructive witness are stronger and not supplied by the inspected predecessor statements.
residual_risks: A general earlier constraint-satisfaction exchange theorem for at-most-two-occurrence convex binary systems might imply the gap-free property.
